children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange were rising on Tuesday morning, mainly on gains from crude oil, while a stronger Canadian dollar put pressure on the oilseed. There was no trading on Monday due to Labor Day.

Renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran, as well as attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Saudi Arabia, caused crude-oil prices to gain more than US$1 per barrel this morning. Chicago soyoil was up, while European rapeseed was mixed and Malaysian palm oil was down.

Rainfall warnings were in effect for southeastern Alberta as well as in central and southwestern Saskatchewan this morning, including in Lethbridge and Saskatoon. Except for southern Manitoba, the Prairies will see rain and cooler temperatures.
The Canadian dollar was up three-tenths of a U.S. cent compared with Friday's close. Canada's counter-tariffs on some U.S. goods came into effect earlier today.
Nearly 19,600 contracts were traded. Prices in Canadian dollars per metric ton as of 9:54 a.m. ET:

Price      Change 
Nov       832.40     up 9.90 
Jan       842.30     up 9.60 
Mar       850.20     up 8.80 
May       854.60     up 7.90
